ig_caption:
Vienna, 1910. Richard Réti had White against Savielly Tartakower, in a short game played for a small stake, not in a tournament.

It began as a Caro-Kann. Black won a pawn with a queen check, and White calmly castled on the queen's side. Then Black took a knight that looked free. White answered by giving up his queen with check, and a double check from bishop and rook left the king with nowhere safe to go. The oldest reports say Black resigned there; the mate that was coming was 11.Bd8. It is one of the best-known short games ever played.

Would you have taken the knight? 👇

slides.title: Vienna, 1910
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5
slides.take: Richard Réti, White, against Savielly Tartakower: a short game for a small stake. It starts as a Caro-Kann, and White brings the queen out early.
slides.edge: Black strikes back at once with 5...e5, offering a pawn to open lines.

slides.title: A pawn and a plan
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5 dxe5 Qa5+ Bd2 Qxe5 O-O-O
slides.take: Black's queen check wins the pawn back on e5. White does not worry about it and castles on the queen's side.
slides.edge: Now White's rook sits on d1, behind the queen on the open d-file.

slides.title: The free knight
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5 dxe5 Qa5+ Bd2 Qxe5 O-O-O Nxe4
slides.take: 8...Nxe4 takes White's knight. It looks like a free piece.
slides.edge: But Black's king is still on e8, right next to the open d-file. That is what White was waiting for.

slides.title: The queen goes
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5 dxe5 Qa5+ Bd2 Qxe5 O-O-O Nxe4 Qd8+ Kxd8
slides.take: 9.Qd8+ gives the queen away with check. Black must take it with the king.
slides.edge: White is not being careless. The queen's job is to pull the king onto the open d-file.

slides.title: Double check
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5 dxe5 Qa5+ Bd2 Qxe5 O-O-O Nxe4 Qd8+ Kxd8 Bg5+
slides.take: 10.Bg5+ is check from the bishop and, behind it, from the rook on d1. Two checks at once.
slides.edge: You cannot block or capture two checks with one move. The king must move. The oldest reports say Black resigned here.

slides.title: Mate on d8
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5 dxe5 Qa5+ Bd2 Qxe5 O-O-O Nxe4 Qd8+ Kxd8 Bg5+ Kc7 Bd8#
slides.take: If 10...Kc7, then 11.Bd8 is mate. The rook guards the bishop and the d-file; Black's own pieces box the king in.
slides.edge: The lesson: before you take a free piece, look at where your king is standing.
